examples.prompt: Provide the non-compliance report for April 2026
examples.business_meaning: List employees whose KRA goals were not completed during a specific calendar month, filtered by target_date falling within that month

filters.active: u.is_active=1 AND u.is_delete=0 AND ugm.isDelete=0 AND ugm.isactive=1 AND d.is_active=1

examples.sql_pattern: SELECT CONCAT(TRIM(u.firstname),' ',TRIM(u.lastname),' (',u.employee_id,')') AS employee, d.designation_name, u.stream AS department, mg.goal_desc AS goal_name, s.status_name AS goal_status, ugm.target_date FROM user_goal_mapping ugm JOIN user_table u ON ugm.employee_id = u.employee_id JOIN designation d ON u.designation_id = d.designation_id JOIN master_goals mg ON ugm.goal_id = mg.goal_id LEFT JOIN status s ON ugm.status_id = s.id WHERE u.is_active=1 AND u.is_delete=0 AND ugm.isDelete=0 AND ugm.isactive=1 AND d.is_active=1 AND s.status_name != 'Completed' AND YEAR(ugm.target_date) = 2026 AND MONTH(ugm.target_date) = 4 ORDER BY u.stream, u.firstname

examples.prompt: Provide the non-compliance report for April 2026, categorized department-wise
examples.business_meaning: Count of non-compliant employees and incomplete goals per department (u.stream) for a specific month — aggregate summary grouped by stream

filters.grouping: GROUP BY u.stream ORDER BY non_compliant_employees DESC

examples.sql_pattern: SELECT u.stream AS department, COUNT(DISTINCT ugm.employee_id) AS non_compliant_employees, COUNT(ugm.id) AS incomplete_goals FROM user_goal_mapping ugm JOIN user_table u ON ugm.employee_id = u.employee_id JOIN designation d ON u.designation_id = d.designation_id JOIN master_goals mg ON ugm.goal_id = mg.goal_id LEFT JOIN status s ON ugm.status_id = s.id WHERE u.is_active=1 AND u.is_delete=0 AND ugm.isDelete=0 AND ugm.isactive=1 AND d.is_active=1 AND s.status_name != 'Completed' AND YEAR(ugm.target_date) = 2026 AND MONTH(ugm.target_date) = 4 GROUP BY u.stream ORDER BY non_compliant_employees DESC

examples.prompt: Share the feedback report for 2026, including inputs from the employee, reporting manager, and HR

filters.active: u.is_active=1 AND u.is_delete=0 AND ugm.isDelete=0 AND ugm.isactive=1 AND d.is_active=1

examples.prompt: List all employees who directly report to Jerome
examples.business_meaning: Employees whose reporting_manager resolves to a named manager — self-join on user_table to match manager by first or last name
examples.sql_pattern: SELECT CONCAT(TRIM(u.firstname),' ',TRIM(u.lastname),' (',u.employee_id,')') AS employee, d.designation_name, u.stream, u.e_mail, CONCAT(TRIM(mgr.firstname),' ',TRIM(mgr.lastname)) AS reporting_manager FROM user_table u JOIN designation d ON u.designation_id = d.designation_id JOIN user_table mgr ON u.reporting_manager = mgr.employee_id WHERE u.is_active=1 AND u.is_delete=0 AND d.is_active=1 AND (mgr.firstname LIKE '%Jerome%' OR mgr.lastname LIKE '%Jerome%') ORDER BY u.firstname

examples.prompt: List employees who have not been reviewed in the last 6 months
examples.business_meaning: Employees with no manager remarks (remarks_table) in the past 6 months — LEFT JOIN with date-bounded ON clause, HAVING last_reviewed_at IS NULL
joins: remarks_table rt ON u.employee_id = rt.user_id AND rt.created_at >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 6 MONTH)
examples.sql_pattern: SELECT CONCAT(TRIM(u.firstname),' ',TRIM(u.lastname),' (',u.employee_id,')') AS employee, d.designation_name, u.stream, MAX(rt.created_at) AS last_reviewed_at FROM user_table u JOIN designation d ON u.designation_id = d.designation_id LEFT JOIN remarks_table rt ON u.employee_id = rt.user_id AND rt.created_at >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 6 MONTH) WHERE u.is_active=1 AND u.is_delete=0 AND d.is_active=1 GROUP BY u.employee_id, u.firstname, u.lastname, d.designation_name, u.stream HAVING last_reviewed_at IS NULL ORDER BY u.stream, u.firstname

examples.prompt: Give me a report of all employees in the QA stream.
examples.business_meaning: List active employees belonging to a specific stream/department — user_table.stream stores a tag_id, so the tags table must be joined to resolve the human-readable stream name. Filter using tags.tag LIKE '%<stream>%', never compare u.stream directly to a string.
examples.stream_join_rule: user_table.stream stores a numeric tag_id. Always join: user_table u LEFT JOIN tags t ON t.tag_id = u.stream. Display t.tag AS stream. Filter with t.tag LIKE '%<name>%'. Never use u.stream = '<name>'.
examples.sql_pattern: SELECT u.firstname, u.lastname, u.employee_id, u.designation, t.tag AS stream FROM user_table u LEFT JOIN tags t ON t.tag_id = u.stream WHERE t.tag LIKE '%QA%' AND u.is_active=1 AND u.is_delete=0 ORDER BY u.firstname

examples.prompt: Show all employees in the Dev stream.
examples.business_meaning: Same stream-lookup pattern as stream_employees_by_stream_name — the stream name in the WHERE clause changes to match the requested stream. Always join tags on tag_id; never filter on the raw u.stream column.
examples.stream_join_rule: user_table.stream stores a numeric tag_id. Always join: user_table u LEFT JOIN tags t ON t.tag_id = u.stream. Display t.tag AS stream. Filter with t.tag LIKE '%<name>%'. Never use u.stream = '<name>'.
examples.sql_pattern: SELECT u.firstname, u.lastname, u.employee_id, u.designation, t.tag AS stream FROM user_table u LEFT JOIN tags t ON t.tag_id = u.stream WHERE t.tag LIKE '%Dev%' AND u.is_active=1 AND u.is_delete=0 ORDER BY u.firstname

examples.prompt: Build a report of all employees with number of goals not filled for May 2026.
examples.business_meaning: Per-employee count of goals that have NO entry in remarks_table for May 2026. Uses INNER JOIN user_goal_mapping + LEFT JOIN remarks_table + WHERE rt.id IS NULL. Employees with all goals remarked automatically disappear (no 0-count rows). COUNT(DISTINCT ugm.id) counts only unremarked goals.

filters.active: u.is_active=1 AND u.is_delete=0 AND ugm.isDelete=0 AND ugm.isactive=1 AND d.is_active=1

critical_rules: INNER JOIN user_goal_mapping — NOT LEFT JOIN
LEFT JOIN remarks_table rt ON ugm.goal_id = rt.goal_id
WHERE rt.id IS NULL — the key filter that finds goals with no remark
No HAVING needed — WHERE rt.id IS NULL naturally removes employees with 0 missing
NEVER use CASE WHEN s.status_name != 'Completed' for this query type
examples.sql_pattern: SELECT CONCAT(TRIM(u.firstname),' ',TRIM(u.lastname),' (',u.employee_id,')') AS employee, d.designation_name, t.tag AS stream, COUNT(DISTINCT ugm.id) AS goals_not_filled FROM user_table u JOIN user_goal_mapping ugm ON u.employee_id = ugm.employee_id JOIN designation d ON u.designation_id = d.designation_id LEFT JOIN tags t ON t.tag_id = u.stream LEFT JOIN remarks_table rt ON ugm.goal_id = rt.goal_id WHERE u.is_active = 1 AND u.is_delete = 0 AND ugm.isDelete = 0 AND ugm.isactive = 1 AND d.is_active = 1 AND rt.id IS NULL AND MONTH(ugm.target_date) = 5 AND YEAR(ugm.target_date) = 2026 GROUP BY u.employee_id, u.firstname, u.lastname, d.designation_name, t.tag ORDER BY goals_not_filled DESC, employee

examples.prompt: Build a report of all employees with missing remarks.
examples.business_meaning: Same as goals_not_filled_per_employee_month but without a date filter — all-time missing remarks. INNER JOIN + LEFT JOIN remarks_table + WHERE rt.id IS NULL. No date condition.

filters.active: u.is_active=1 AND u.is_delete=0 AND ugm.isDelete=0 AND ugm.isactive=1 AND d.is_active=1

examples.sql_pattern: SELECT CONCAT(TRIM(u.firstname),' ',TRIM(u.lastname),' (',u.employee_id,')') AS employee, d.designation_name, t.tag AS stream, COUNT(DISTINCT ugm.id) AS goals_not_filled FROM user_table u JOIN user_goal_mapping ugm ON u.employee_id = ugm.employee_id JOIN designation d ON u.designation_id = d.designation_id LEFT JOIN tags t ON t.tag_id = u.stream LEFT JOIN remarks_table rt ON ugm.goal_id = rt.goal_id WHERE u.is_active = 1 AND u.is_delete = 0 AND ugm.isDelete = 0 AND ugm.isactive = 1 AND d.is_active = 1 AND rt.id IS NULL GROUP BY u.employee_id, u.firstname, u.lastname, d.designation_name, t.tag ORDER BY goals_not_filled DESC, employee

examples.prompt: How many employees have zero filled remarks this month?
examples.business_meaning: SCALAR COUNT of active employees who have not submitted any remark in the current calendar month. The outer SELECT must be COUNT(*) AS employee_count — NEVER a list of employee names. Use a subquery: inner query groups by employee and applies HAVING COUNT(rt.id) = 0; outer query counts qualifying rows.
joins: remarks_table rt ON u.employee_id = rt.user_id AND MONTH(rt.enteredDate) = MONTH(CURDATE()) AND YEAR(rt.enteredDate) = YEAR(CURDATE())
examples.sql_pattern: SELECT COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM (SELECT u.employee_id FROM user_table u LEFT JOIN remarks_table rt ON u.employee_id = rt.user_id AND MONTH(rt.enteredDate) = MONTH(CURDATE()) AND YEAR(rt.enteredDate) = YEAR(CURDATE()) WHERE u.is_active = 1 AND u.is_delete = 0 GROUP BY u.employee_id HAVING COUNT(rt.id) = 0) AS zero_remark_employees

examples.prompt: How many employees have completed all their KRA goals this month?
examples.business_meaning: SCALAR COUNT — single number answer. Inner subquery finds employees who have zero incomplete goals this month using HAVING; outer query counts them. NEVER return a list of names for a 'how many' query.

filters.active: u.is_active = 1 AND u.is_delete = 0 AND ugm.isDelete = 0 AND ugm.isactive = 1
filters.having: HAVING COUNT(CASE WHEN s.status_name != 'Completed' THEN 1 END) = 0

examples.sql_pattern: SELECT COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM (SELECT u.employee_id FROM user_goal_mapping ugm JOIN user_table u ON ugm.employee_id = u.employee_id LEFT JOIN status s ON ugm.status_id = s.id WHERE u.is_active = 1 AND u.is_delete = 0 AND ugm.isDelete = 0 AND ugm.isactive = 1 AND MONTH(ugm.target_date) = MONTH(CURDATE()) AND YEAR(ugm.target_date) = YEAR(CURDATE()) GROUP BY u.employee_id HAVING COUNT(CASE WHEN s.status_name != 'Completed' THEN 1 END) = 0) AS fully_completed_employees

examples.business_meaning: Aggregate count of active employees grouped by stream/department — join tags to resolve the readable stream name from user_table.stream (tag_id), group by t.tag, order by count descending.

filters.grouping: GROUP BY t.tag ORDER BY employee_count DESC

examples.stream_join_rule: user_table.stream stores a numeric tag_id. Always join: user_table u LEFT JOIN tags t ON t.tag_id = u.stream. Display t.tag AS stream. Filter with t.tag LIKE '%<name>%'. Never use u.stream = '<name>'.
examples.sql_pattern: SELECT t.tag AS stream, COUNT(u.employee_id) AS employee_count FROM user_table u LEFT JOIN tags t ON t.tag_id = u.stream WHERE u.is_active=1 AND u.is_delete=0 GROUP BY t.tag ORDER BY employee_count DESC

stream_sql_rules.description: Rules that govern SQL generation for any prompt about streams, departments, or stream-wise employee data.
stream_sql_rules.schema_prerequisite: Verify that both user_table.stream and tags.tag_id exist in kra_schema_llm_context.json before applying these rules. If the tags table is unavailable, ask a schema-grounded clarification instead of generating SQL.
stream_sql_rules.join_required: user_table u LEFT JOIN tags t ON t.tag_id = u.stream
rules: For any stream-related prompt, do NOT return user_table.stream directly.
Always join: user_table u LEFT JOIN tags t ON t.tag_id = u.stream
Display stream using: t.tag AS stream
Filter stream values using: t.tag LIKE '%<stream_name>%'
Do not display numeric stream IDs unless explicitly requested.
Use the stream few-shot examples (stream_employees_by_stream_name, stream_employees_dev, stream_employee_count) as the default reference for all stream/department queries.
Keep existing employee display and report rendering logic unchanged.
If tags table is unavailable in schema, ask schema-grounded clarification instead of generating fake SQL.
